### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c87e2ad2c0b53946ee0025bf58efa93d44874354` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `357c57c9bb7dabf41597f90efb6a040211f348f7` — the merge of head `ab873a6a406d43b5a716efb9fb72ba921c19f862` into base `c87e2ad2c0b53946ee0025bf58efa93d44874354`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 357c57c9bb7dabf41597f90efb6a040211f348f7 && git checkout 357c57c9bb7dabf41597f90efb6a040211f348f7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c87e2ad2c0b53946ee0025bf58efa93d44874354 ab873a6a406d43b5a716efb9fb72ba921c19f862 && git checkout -B drift-repro c87e2ad2c0b53946ee0025bf58efa93d44874354 && git merge --no-ff ab873a6a406d43b5a716efb9fb72ba921c19f862

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c87e2ad2c0b53946ee0025bf58efa93d44874354
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `ab873a6a406d43b5a716efb9fb72ba921c19f862`
Reviewer: review-c (areas S5 + S6) · read 2026-11-15T12:57Z
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jUZKdq3PK2Sab53cT3 · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

Read at the head on GitHub: all 7 files of the diff against merge base `b0056382`, card #33500 and #33380 in full, `ExecutionStepLogSchema` / `FlowRunNodeSummarySchema` `warnings` in `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts`, the package `exports` map and `src/index.ts`, and a whole-tree grep for readers of the old notify text.

1. **#33500 item 1 (stable notify text).** `deliveryFailureWarning` drops the count from all three spots and keeps one entry per (channel, reason) in first-seen order. `failed` is still read, for the early return, so no dead variable is left behind. The counts really are on the node output (`notify-node.ts` returns `delivered` / `enqueued` / `failed`). Old-text readers in the tree: none. The only hits are the historical `CHANGELOG.md` line and a literal fixture in `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.test.ts:468` (see nit 2). The loop integration case has a real control (the `emit` spy reads failed 1, 2, 3), so the "one text" assertion is not green by accident.
2. **#33500 item 2 (per-text bound).** `boundedWarning` is applied before `seen.add`, so the fold and the 5-entry cap count the cut texts. The arithmetic holds: the marker is 44 units, so the cut keeps 256 and the result is 300. The surrogate guard steps back one unit when the last kept unit is a high surrogate, which gives 299, not 300. The test asserts the kept prefix, not the length, and that is correct. The at-bound case is the positive control. Item 3 (`warningsOmitted`) was left out, as the card allows ("leave it out if (1) and (2) are enough"), so `Fixes #33500` is right.
3. **#33380 (type pin + docblock).** `AdvisoryKeys` uses the same invariant `Eq` as the region keys. Both sides declare `warnings?: string[]` and `droppedFields?: DroppedFieldsEvent[]`. The comment now names `nodeLabel` as the only engine-local member. The `stepAdvisoriesOf` sentence now says what the code does (the `fields: []` shape is the one divergence), and the card offers that route ("or narrow the sentence"). `Fixes #33380` is right.
4. **Ablations.** The body records four, each restored to HEAD. The type pin was caught by a narrow mutation, with the exact TS2344 at `region-index-keys.test.ts(76,5)`; the body also explains why the wider `unknown[]` mutation did not isolate the pin. Count restored: red. Bound removed: red, length 1217 against 300. Surrogate guard removed: red. Every new negative pin has a recorded red.
5. **Clause-② no / Metadata-protocol none: right.** No schema moves. `MAX_NODE_SUMMARY_WARNING_LENGTH` and `NODE_SUMMARY_WARNING_CUT_MARKER` are exported from `run-summary.ts` only. `src/index.ts` re-exports just `summarizeRun` and `formatRunSummaryLine`, and `exports` has only `.`, so nothing new is addressable. Leaving the dependents' suites to CI is sound for that reason. The patch changeset is on a published package. Each sentence was checked against the diff: "carries no count", the two quoted new texts (verbatim from the code), "The counts stay where they were…", "cut at 300 characters, ending with ` [... cut; the step log holds the full text]`", "Two long texts that agree up to the cut fold into one entry", and "fallback drops the whole node list" (`detailOmitted`). All true. File surface: service-automation only, inside the S6 paths.
6. **Gates not judged.** At review time 17 check-runs were in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Lint, Type Check), 17 succeeded and 18 were skipped, with none red. Landing needs every check green on this head.

**Nits (no must-fix, no should-fix):**

- N1. The changeset says "300 characters", but the code bounds UTF-16 code units, and a cut beside an astral character keeps 299. This is accepted wording, not a defect.
- N2 → **follow-up card owed (spec lane, p3)**. The published `describe` on `FlowRunNodeSummarySchema.warnings` does not mention the new per-text cut, so it still reads as if each entry were a raised text. The body says so and keeps `packages/spec` out of bounds, and that is right for this PR: a `packages/spec` edit is the schema face and owes a CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record. The `describe` sentence plus the stale count-bearing fixture at `execution.test.ts:468` belong in one spec card. Please file it and name it on #33500 before landing.
